message: User requested a full visual polish pass for the public landing page and the in-app chatbot. Please prioritize cleaner hierarchy, stronger uniformity, better responsiveness, and reduced visual congestion while preserving the existing backend capabilities and workspace edit flow.

landingPage: Simplify the visual system to match the monochrome professional app direction more closely.
Reduce the number of competing accent colors. Current feature cards use many unrelated accent hues, which makes the page feel less premium and less uniform.
Tone down motion intensity: the rotating headline word, multiple animated glow orbs, magnetic CTA, and hover-reactive gradients are individually fine but collectively too busy.
Keep one clear hero, one concise value section, one trust band, and one closing CTA. The current page is strong structurally but needs calmer visual restraint.
Normalize card radii, spacing rhythm, and text density so the hero, feature bento, trust cards, and CTA feel designed as one system rather than adjacent sections.
Keep the dashboard preview, but make it feel more product-real and less decorative so the page looks more credible.
Check footer typography and symbol rendering carefully. There are signs of encoding inconsistency in rendered text output.
chatbot: Fix compact-height usability. In small window sizes the assistant becomes too congested and hard to scroll comfortably.
Reduce duplicate status chips and repeated context labels. The header, subheader, body, and footer repeat the same ideas too many times.
Make the default compact state calmer: tighter but cleaner spacing, fewer stacked pills, and better breathing room around messages and input.
Ensure the history pane behaves well on small screens. It should not crowd the message area or create multiple competing scroll regions.
Strengthen responsive rules for narrow desktop and tablet widths so the panel stays readable without overlap or clipped affordances.
Upgrade message rendering polish: clearer assistant/user separation, cleaner timestamps, smoother loading state, and less visual noise in the empty state.
Preserve saved chat history, workspace edits, and backend response handling already implemented by Codex.

technicalNotes: Files remain Antigravity-owned: src/components/landing-page.tsx, src/components/career-assistant.tsx, src/app/globals.css.
Backend resume, digest, and assistant routes are already live on codex/work and do not require UI contract changes for this polish pass.
Current chatbot code still shows MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES = 8 in the component; please reconcile UI assumptions with the intended lightweight focused-mode behavior.
Please preserve the existing API routes and assistant action flow. The visual pass should not break workspace refresh after actions are applied.
acceptanceCriteria: Landing page feels calmer, more premium, and more consistent with the monochrome workspace direction.
Chatbot is comfortably usable in compact height/width scenarios without cramped scrolling or overlapping regions.
Animations remain smooth but are noticeably less busy and more intentional.
Typography, spacing, and card treatments feel uniform across both surfaces.
No regressions to auth routes, assistant history, assistant actions, or existing backend integrations.
